### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 94b0314c80eed17bdf2d656e317125da6249d9f5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2f473b2d08650557a230c0956bee22a184fbe33f` — the merge of head `13f32fc828a388ed7188f0ec6a5e3ed042013a71` into base `94b0314c80eed17bdf2d656e317125da6249d9f5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2f473b2d08650557a230c0956bee22a184fbe33f && git checkout 2f473b2d08650557a230c0956bee22a184fbe33f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 94b0314c80eed17bdf2d656e317125da6249d9f5 13f32fc828a388ed7188f0ec6a5e3ed042013a71 && git checkout -B drift-repro 94b0314c80eed17bdf2d656e317125da6249d9f5 && git merge --no-ff 13f32fc828a388ed7188f0ec6a5e3ed042013a71

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 94b0314c80eed17bdf2d656e317125da6249d9f5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 94b0314c80eed17bdf2d656e317125da6249d9f5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**Shape and gates.** `l1-face --pr 37951`: CLEAN, 13 items, none flagged. Check-runs at 13f32fc828: 39 success, 18 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending; mergeable_state clean. 3 files, +42/-1. Not governed. `Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none`.

**Item 1, one boot line: delivered.** `buildSourcesAtBoot` now returns early for `trigger === 'boot'` when `this.adapters` has no entry for the source's adapter, before `readIndexStateOf`, so the 'unreadable' warn no longer follows. Both readers run in `kernel:bootstrapped`, after every store's `start()` has registered its adapter, so the skip and `reportUnmountedAdapters` read the same adapter map, and a source skipped here is always the one the error line names. Reload is untouched, so a source loaded later is still named at `warn` by its reload build. The new pin collects every level and asserts exactly one line naming `'docs'`, at `error`, carrying the adapter and "is not mounted". It also proves the mounted source is still built by the same pass. The ablation gives 2 lines.

**Item 2, the publish-time refusal: closed by decision D, accepted.** The card's Done-when leaves the refusal point to the lane and names boot as an allowed one. On this head the rest of Done-when already holds on `main` from #37442, with pins in `knowledge-service.test.ts`. The boot `error` line names the source, the adapter, the mounted choices and the code. `searchWithRefusals` lists the source as refused (`SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, :2291). Index and search answer the coded 503 (:2280). The re-scope's item 2 was a hand-off to #37304 or #37307 "whichever lands first", not a new bar, and D records why boot suffices. Options A (save-time admission) and B (the `ragflow` tombstone) stay in the dev report. Please file A as a follow-up card so it is not lost, since every stored `adapter: 'ragflow'` source lands in this path after #37004.

**Changeset, sentence by sentence.** Named twice before, once at `error` and once at `warn` with the quoted text: true, and it matches the code it removes. "Skips such a source without a line, so the one boot line is the `error`": true. "Indexing and searching ... still answer `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`": true. "A source loaded while the process runs is still named at `warn` by its reload build": true, because the skip is boot-only.

**Body and evidence.** The area's body patch (Fixes, D's acceptance line) is the area's to make under os-dev rule 3. The ablation run outside the verify lock is declared in the PR, the change is 5 lines in one package, and Test Core is green on the head, so it counts.

**Landing:** not governed, under 3000 lines, no narrowing. The area lands it.
